newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends little changed, few business.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends little changed, few business.

text.p: The Malaysian rubber market ended little changed after drifting narrowly, despite scattered business and gains in Tokyo, dealers said.

"Trades were scattered and mainly from Far-East," a dealer said. There was talk that China could have bought small amount of SMR 20 for July shipment on Wednesday but dealers were unable to provide details on price and tonnages.
Turkey and South Korean were also in the market this morning, making inquiries for July SMR 20 rubber. But the market has not heard of any business yet.

"Our (Malaysia) prices are cheap than Thailand and Indonesia and we expect more consumers to commit themseleves in Malaysia stocks," a dealer said. But buyers were still waiting for cheaper levels, they said.
A check with trading houses showed the SMR 20 offered at 258 to 260 cents, SMR CV at 328, SMR L at 307, SMR 10 at 259 and drum latex at 224.
At the close, July RSS1 ended unchanged at Wednesday's 282.50 cents ($1.12) a kg but July SMR 20 was half a cent down at 259.50 cents.
